question: m07
q: What rate are owner-occupiers actually paying on new variable loans, compared with the advertised rate?

transcript.answer:
**Owner-occupiers taking out new variable-rate loans paid about 6.2% in August 2026. That is the latest month available. The advertised rates were higher.**

| Rate, August 2026 | % p.a. |
|---|---|
| Actual rate on new owner-occupier variable loans (RBA F6, all institutions) | **6.2** |
| Advertised discounted variable rate (RBA F5) | 6.8 |
| Advertised standard variable rate (RBA F5) | 8.77 |

- **Discounted rate:** Borrowers paid about 0.6 percentage points less than the advertised discounted rate. That is probably because many get extra discounts beyond the advertised one. The F5 figure for September 2026 is also 6.8%, so the gap is the same on that basis.
- **Standard rate:** Borrowers paid about 2.6 percentage points less than the advertised standard variable rate. Almost nobody pays that rate on a new loan.
- **Large institutions:** The rate on new loans was also 6.2% in August.
- **Existing borrowers:** The average rate across all outstanding owner-occupier variable loans was also 6.2%.

**Trend since the rate rises began**
- The actual new-loan rate was 5.5% from August 2025 to January 2026. It rose to 6.2% by May 2026 and peaked at 6.3% in June 2026 (all institutions). It was 6.2% in July and August.
- The advertised discounted rate went from 6.05% to 6.8% over the same period.
- Rises in the cash rate drove both. The monthly average cash rate went from 3.60% in late 2025 to about 4.36% in September 2026.
- The actual rate rose about 0.7 percentage points from its January 2026 level, and the advertised rate rose 0.75 points. The gap has stayed at roughly 0.6 to 0.7 points.

The F6 figures are rounded to one decimal place, so small differences in the gap may reflect rounding.
